qualifying_findings.title: argocd-mcp 0.8.0 unauthenticated HTTP transport exposes Argo CD tool authority

visible_dates.note: Older upstream advisory; NVD publication is the in-window visible database event.

qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: NVD published CVE-2026-82456 for argocd-mcp 0.8.0. The HTTP transport binds to all network interfaces and allows MCP sessions without inbound caller authentication when ARGOCD_API_TOKEN is configured, so a reachable attacker can invoke tools using the operator's stored Argo CD token.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: primary vulnerability database plus upstream project security advisory and reproducible advisory detail
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: argocd-mcp 0.8.0; patched version reported as 0.9.0 in the GitHub advisory; exposed boundary crosses from MCP listener to Argo CD and Kubernetes resources reachable by the stored token.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: It is a concrete MCP delegated-authority failure: an AI tool server turns an outbound infrastructure credential into unauthenticated inbound control of deployment actions.

upstream_routing.security_wiki: Create or update a local agent-and-tool-security or identity-and-access leaf for MCP inbound authentication, token directionality, host/origin validation, and deployment-tool authority.
upstream_routing.ai_wiki: If needed, route broad argocd-mcp and MCP server catalog facts upstream rather than duplicating them here.
upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki: If needed, route general developer-tool MCP deployment practice upstream; keep the security failure local.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence for the in-window NVD publication and affected boundary. GitHub advisory predates the window, so it is supporting evidence rather than the qualifying date source.
follow_up_actions: During ingest, deduplicate against existing MCP transport and delegated credential pages.

qualifying_findings.title: iFlytek astron-agent workflow copy endpoint misses ownership validation
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: NVD published CVE-2026-82475 for iFlytek astron-agent through 1.1.1. The copyFlow endpoint fails to validate workflow ownership, allowing authenticated attackers to enumerate workflow identifiers and overwrite or copy other tenants' workflows to read their definitions.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: primary vulnerability database with upstream code and issue references
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: iFlytek astron-agent through 1.1.1; authenticated cross-tenant workflow ownership and integrity boundary.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Agent workflow definitions encode delegated actions, model/tool orchestration, and possibly secret-bearing configuration; cross-tenant copy or overwrite is an authorization failure in an AI agent control plane.

upstream_routing.security_wiki: Local identity-and-access and agent-and-tool-security coverage should focus on workflow ownership checks and tenant isolation for agent control planes.
upstream_routing.ai_wiki: Route broad astron-agent product or company background upstream if it becomes durable.
upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki: Route general workflow-authoring practice upstream only if non-security guidance is needed.

qualifying_findings.title: HEL Online Classroom AI WordPress plugin exposes classroom settings and moderator joins
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: NVD published three CVEs for HEL Online Classroom: AI-powered Online Classrooms WordPress plugin through 1.0.3. The plugin lacks authorization on REST routes, allowing unauthenticated retrieval of stored settings and BigBlueButton signing secrets, unauthenticated settings overwrite to repoint classrooms, and unauthenticated signed meeting join links with moderator privileges.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: primary vulnerability database with WPScan advisory references
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: HEL Online Classroom: AI-powered Online Classrooms WordPress plugin through 1.0.3; WordPress REST API to BigBlueButton classroom integration boundary.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: AI-labeled educational plugins can become credential and meeting-authority bridges; missing authorization exposes shared secrets and lets unauthenticated users take over AI-assisted classroom sessions.

upstream_routing.security_wiki: Local identity-and-access and data-and-privacy coverage should focus on plugin REST authorization, shared meeting secrets, and moderator privilege issuance.
upstream_routing.ai_wiki: Route broad WordPress plugin/product catalog detail upstream only if this plugin becomes a recurring AI product entity.
upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki: No general AI-assisted development practice routing identified.

qualifying_findings.title: HEL Online Classroom access-code bypass grants moderator classroom joins
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: CVE-2026-77010 reports that HEL Online Classroom through 1.0.3 does not consistently enforce per-class access codes and does not authorize REST routes, allowing unauthenticated users to obtain signed join links, including moderator-privilege links.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: primary vulnerability database with WPScan advisory reference
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: HEL Online Classroom WordPress plugin through 1.0.3; class access-code and moderator join-signature boundary.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: The finding is the highest-impact member of the HEL cluster because it turns an AI classroom integration into unauthorized privileged session access, not just configuration exposure.

upstream_routing.security_wiki: If the cluster is split, this belongs under identity-and-access as access-code enforcement and delegated session role issuance.
upstream_routing.ai_wiki: Do not duplicate broad plugin catalog facts unless upstream lacks the entity and it becomes recurrent.

qualifying_findings.title: NIST Cybersecurity Insights frames agentic AI as an identity and authorization problem
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: A NIST Cybersecurity Insights post says agentic AI deployments are repeating a pattern of prioritizing features over security and highlights identity and authorization challenges, including overbroad tokens, granular authorization, zero trust, just-in-time access, and least standing privilege for agents whose speed and scale exceed human activity.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: official standards-agency cybersecurity blog with in-window HTTP last-modified evidence
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Enterprise agentic AI identity, authentication, authorization, and least-privilege control design; not a CVE or patch advisory.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: It is official guidance signal that agent security should be governed with identity and authorization foundations rather than relying on model-only guardrails.

upstream_routing.security_wiki: Local identity-and-access and governance-and-compliance pages should capture the agent identity, authorization, least privilege, and audit-evidence implications.
upstream_routing.ai_wiki: Broad NIST organization context remains upstream-owned if needed.
upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki: General agent operating-practice implications can route to ai-dev-wiki, but this repository owns the security-control lens.
